_doc: Sourced US list prices (monthly, new subscribers) for evergreen price-history sections on service pages. date = YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD when the change took effect for new subscribers. Add rows only with a source.

Netflix.intro: Netflix has raised US prices roughly every one to two years since it split streaming from DVD rentals in 2011. Its main ad-free plan (Standard) has gone from $7.99 to $19.99 a month, and that plan has never gotten cheaper.

latest.what: all three US plans went up: Standard with ads $7.99 to $8.99, Standard $17.99 to $19.99, Premium $24.99 to $26.99. Extra members rose to $7.99 (with ads) and $9.99 (ad-free).

notes: Basic closed to new US members on July 19, 2023 and ended for remaining members on July 18, 2024.
The 2014 increase applied to new members first; existing members kept $7.99 for a period.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)
Dormant: streaming price history (dated flagship prices)

Spotify.intro: Spotify Premium Individual cost $9.99 a month in the US for twelve years, from its 2011 launch until July 2023. It has gone up three times since, and is now $12.99.

latest.what: Spotify announced US increases to Individual $12.99, Duo $18.99, and Family $21.99, with existing subscribers notified by email over the following month. Our own daily snapshot of spotify.com/us/premium shows these prices today.

notes: Family launched in 2014 at $14.99 for two people (more for extra members); in May 2016 it became $14.99 for up to six.
Student was $5.99 after both the 2023 and 2024 increases.

Disney+.intro: Disney+ launched in the US at $6.99 a month in November 2019. The ad-free plan is now $21.49, up more than 200%, with at least one price increase every year since 2022.

latest.what: ad-free Disney+ Premium went from $18.99 to $21.49 and Disney+ with ads from $11.99 to $12.49 for new subscribers; existing subscribers moved to the new price on their next monthly bill.

notes: The September 2026 change also raised the ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle from $19.99 to $21.99; the bundle with ads stayed at $12.99.

Hulu.intro: Hulu's ad-free plan launched at $11.99 a month in 2015 and is now $21.49, after five increases. The plan with ads, which Hulu cut to $5.99 in 2019, has since doubled to $12.49.

latest.what: Hulu (No Ads) went from $18.99 to $21.49 and Hulu with ads from $11.99 to $12.49 for new subscribers, with existing subscribers moving to the new rates at their next billing date. The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads stayed at $12.99.

notes: The 2010 rows are Hulu Plus, the paid ad-supported plan; Hulu's free ad-supported site ran separately until 2016.
Disney took full ownership of Hulu in 2025 and plans to fold Hulu's content into Disney+; bundle prices are not tracked here.
Hulu + Live TV is a separate product and not included in these tables.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)

Peacock.intro: Peacock has raised prices every summer since 2023. Its main plan, Premium (with ads), launched at $4.99 a month in July 2020 and is now $12.99, more than two and a half times the launch price.

latest.what: Premium went from $10.99 to $12.99, Premium Plus from $16.99 to $19.99, and Select from $7.99 to $8.99 a month for new subscribers. People who subscribed before Aug 18 moved to the new prices at their first billing date on or after Sep 17.

notes: Peacock's free tier closed to new members in 2023.
Select (launched July 2025) is a cheaper tier with NBC and Bravo shows but no movies, live sports or Peacock originals.
Annual plans also rose on Aug 18, 2026: Select $89.99, Premium $129.99, Premium Plus $199.99 a year.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)

YouTube.name: YouTube Premium
YouTube.intro: YouTube's ad-free subscription launched as YouTube Red at $9.99 a month in 2015. Renamed YouTube Premium in 2018, the individual plan is now $15.99, and the family plan has gone from $17.99 to $26.99 since 2022.

latest.what: YouTube Premium Individual went from $13.99 to $15.99, Family from $22.99 to $26.99, and Premium Lite from $7.99 to $8.99 a month. New sign-ups paid the new prices right away; existing subscribers were emailed and moved over at a later billing date. The annual individual plan went from $139.99 to $159.99.

notes: The 2015 price is YouTube Red, which became YouTube Premium in June 2018.
Prices are for paying on YouTube's website; subscribing through Apple's App Store costs more.
Premium Lite removes most ads but doesn't include YouTube Music, background play or downloads.
sources: Ars Technica, Apr 2026 (Red and Premium launch prices)

Amazon Prime.intro: Amazon Prime launched at $79 a year in 2005 and now costs $139 a year or $14.99 a month. Amazon has raised the membership about every four years, most recently in February 2022, and has not announced an increase in 2026.

latest.what: Prime went from $119 to $139 a year and from $12.99 to $14.99 a month for new members. Ad-free Prime Video costs extra on top of that: $2.99 a month from January 2024, renamed Prime Video Ultra at $4.99 a month in April 2026.

notes: Amazon's help page lists today's prices: $14.99 a month, $139 a year, Prime Video alone $8.99 a month, Prime for Young Adults $7.49 a month or $69 a year.
Analysts have predicted a 2026 increase to about $159 a year; Amazon has not confirmed one.
sources: Amazon Customer Service: The Amazon Prime Membership Fee
Streaming Price Tracker: Prime Video history

HBO Max.intro: HBO Max launched in May 2020 at $14.99 a month with no ads. It became Max in May 2023 and HBO Max again in July 2025. The ad-free Standard plan is now $18.49, the 4K Premium plan $22.99, and the ad-supported plan $10.99, after the latest increase on October 21, 2025.

latest.what: HBO Max raised every plan: Basic with Ads from $9.99 to $10.99, Standard from $16.99 to $18.49 and Premium from $20.99 to $22.99 a month. New subscribers paid the new prices right away; existing monthly subscribers moved over at their first billing date on or after November 20, 2025.

notes: Plan names have changed with the brand: the ad-supported plan was HBO Max With Ads, then Max Ad-Lite, now Basic with Ads; Standard was the Ad-Free plan; Premium was Max Ultimate Ad Free, added when Max launched on May 23, 2023.
Max was renamed back to HBO Max on July 9, 2025, with no change to plans or prices.

After Paramount Skydance completed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison said on October 7, 2026 that HBO Max and Paramount+ will be run separately for now and combined over time. No price change for HBO Max has been announced.
Current prices from HBO Max's own plans page: Basic with Ads $10.99/month or $109.99/year, Standard $18.49 or $184.99, Premium $22.99 or $229.99, before tax.
sources: HBO Max help: plans and prices (current prices)
HBO Max help: price changes, Oct 2025 (annual prices, dates)
Warner Bros. Discovery, Apr 12, 2023 (Max launch prices)
TechCrunch, Jan 12, 2023 ($14.99 to $15.99, first increase since May 2020)
WBD Pressroom: HBO Max is back (Jul 2025)

Paramount+.intro: Paramount+ replaced CBS All Access on March 4, 2021, with an ad-free plan at $9.99 a month, and added a $4.99 ad-supported Essential plan that June. After three increases to each plan, Essential is $8.99 and the ad-free Premium plan is $13.99, both raised on January 15, 2026.

latest.what: Paramount+ Essential went from $7.99 to $8.99 and Premium from $12.99 to $13.99 a month. Annual plans rose more: Essential from $59.99 to $89.99 a year and Premium from $119.99 to $139.99.

notes: Premium was called Paramount+ with Showtime from June 27, 2023 (it replaced the $9.99 ad-free plan at $11.99) until 2025, when it was renamed Paramount+ Premium.
The $4.99 Essential plan replaced CBS All Access's $5.99 plan with commercials and, unlike it, left out live local CBS stations.
In August 2024, existing monthly Essential subscribers kept $5.99; the $7.99 price applied to new subscribers.

After Paramount Skydance completed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison said on October 7, 2026 that Paramount+ and HBO Max will be run separately for now and combined over time. No new Paramount+ price has been announced.
Current monthly prices ($8.99 Essential, $13.99 Premium) confirmed on paramountplus.com on October 19, 2026.

Apple TV.intro: Apple TV+ launched in November 2019 at $4.99 a month and was renamed Apple TV in October 2025. It has now gone up four times, most recently to $14.99 a month and $119 a year on August 28, 2026, three times its launch price.

latest.what: Apple TV went from $12.99 to $14.99 a month and from $99 to $119 a year, and Apple One Individual from $19.95 to $21.95. New subscribers paid the new price right away; Apple said existing subscribers would be notified about a month before being charged it.

notes: Apple dropped the plus and renamed Apple TV+ to Apple TV on October 13, 2025. Prices didn't change with the rename.
The annual plan stayed at $99 when the monthly price went to $12.99 in August 2025, then rose to $119 in August 2026.
Apple TV is also included in Apple One bundles, which start at $21.95 a month (Individual) as of October 2026.
Current $14.99 monthly price confirmed on apple.com on October 19, 2026.
sources: MacRumors, Oct 25, 2023 ($6.99 to $9.99, $69 to $99 a year)
The New York Times, Oct 13, 2025 (rename to Apple TV)

Slack.title: Slack pricing history (2014–2026): every Pro and Business+ price increase
Slack.basis: US list prices per active user per month, before tax, in nominal dollars, for buying on Slack's website. Annual-billing prices are Slack's per-month equivalent. Compiled from the sources below and our daily snapshots of slack.com/pricing; last verified {verified}.
Slack.intro: Slack kept its Pro plan (originally called Standard) at $8 per user a month, or $6.67 billed annually, from its 2014 launch until September 1, 2022. Business+ went from $12.50 to $15 per user a month in 2025, when Salesforce folded AI features into it. Today Pro is $8.75 monthly or $7.25 annually, and Business+ is $18 monthly or $15 annually.

latest.what: Slack raised Business+ from $12.50 to $15 per user a month on annual billing, and from $15 to $18 on monthly billing, adding AI features and Salesforce integrations. Pro prices stayed the same. Business+ customers who bought on Slack's website moved to the new plan at their first renewal after August 17, 2025.

notes: The September 1, 2022 Pro increase was Slack's first since launching in 2014. Annual Pro customers could lock in $6.67 for another year by renewing before that date.
The same day, the Free plan switched from the last 10,000 messages and 5GB of files to the last 90 days of messages and files.

Enterprise+ was added in June 2025 as a contact-sales plan. Since October 15, 2026, Slack's pricing page has sometimes shown it at $45 per user a month and sometimes as 'Contact sales', which looks like a test (see our Slack changelog below).
Turning AI features off doesn't lower the price of a Slack plan, according to Slack's help center.
Enterprise Grid and contracts signed through Slack sales aren't covered here; pricing for those is negotiated.
sources: Slack blog, Jun 17, 2025 (Business+ $12.50 to $15; monthly $15 to $18)
Slack help: updates to feature availability and pricing (Aug 17, 2025 renewals)
The Verge, Jul 19, 2022 (Pro $8 to $8.75, $6.67 to $7.25; Free 90-day limit)
